name: Hungary
description: Hungary, situated in the heart of Eastern Europe, is increasingly appealing to expats due to its affordable cost of living, rich cultural heritage, and a favorable tax system. It offers a high quality of life for a fraction of the cost compared to Western Europe, making it attractive for individuals and families seeking new opportunities or a relaxed retirement.
longdescription: Expat life in Hungary offers a blend of historical charm and modern convenience. Budapest, the capital, is particularly popular with a vibrant expat community, stunning architecture, and a bustling cultural scene, all at a lower cost than many major EU cities. Outside the capital, smaller towns and rural areas provide an even more affordable and laid-back lifestyle. The economy is growing, attracting professionals in IT, shared service centers, and multinational corporations. However, while job opportunities exist, they might be more limited outside specialized sectors, and local salaries can be lower than in Western Europe. The country is generally safe, with a low crime rate, though petty theft can occur in tourist areas. Healthcare is of good quality, with both public and private options available, and private healthcare is notably less expensive than in other Western European countries. Navigating bureaucracy can be a challenge, and the Hungarian language presents a significant barrier for many expats.

visas.name: Digital Nomad Visa (White Card)
visas.description: The Hungary Digital Nomad Visa, officially known as the 'White Card,' is a residence permit for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who wish to live in Hungary while working remotely for an employer or company registered outside Hungary. It allows individuals to reside legally in the country and travel within the Schengen Area while performing their work using digital technologies.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens) who are employed remotely by a foreign company or own a profitable business registered outside Hungary, and who do not intend to pursue gainful activity in Hungary.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The White Card does not directly lead to permanent residency or citizenship in Hungary. After a maximum stay of two years (initial 1-year validity + 1-year renewal), the holder must leave Hungary and reapply for the White Card or apply for a different type of residence permit on other grounds if they wish to return.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit can be renewed once for another year, provided the applicant continues to meet the original eligibility criteria (including income and foreign employment/business ownership) and has genuinely resided in Hungary for at least 90 days within any 180-day period of the current permit. The renewal application is submitted via the Enter Hungary platform.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the White Card are generally not taxed in Hungary on income earned abroad unless they establish tax residency. Individuals who spend at least 183 days in Hungary within a calendar year may become Hungarian tax residents, in which case their worldwide income could be subject to Hungary's 15% personal income tax rate.
benefits: Legal residence in Hungary for remote work.
Visa-free travel within the Schengen Area.
Access to a relatively affordable cost of living in a European Union country.
High-speed internet and developed coworking culture.
Potential tax efficiency on foreign income if not a tax resident (staying less than 183 days).
required_documents: Completed application form and appendix
Valid passport (copy of every page)
Recent ID picture (no older than three months)
Bank account statements for the last 6 months showing EUR 3,000+ monthly income
Proof of current bank account balance (at least €10,000 for savings)
Proof of income (certificate showing at least EUR 3,000 per month for the last six months)
Proof of comprehensive health insurance covering the duration of stay
Proof of accommodation in Hungary (e.g., rental contract, property ownership, or accommodation reservation for at least 12 months)
Proof of remote employment or business ownership outside Hungary (employment contract, service agreement, company ownership documents, letter from employer confirming remote work)
Proof of exit (valid passport AND travel ticket OR sufficient funds for travel)
Certificate of no criminal record from home country
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, including proof of remote employment/business ownership, financial statements, health insurance, and accommodation details.

Submit the application at a Hungarian consulate or embassy in your country of residence (for non-visa-free nationals) or directly within Hungary (for visa-free nationals via Enter Hungary or in person at NDGAP).
Pay the application fee.
Attend a biometric data appointment (facial photograph and fingerprints).
Await approval (typically 21-60 days).

If applying from abroad, receive a Type D visa to enter Hungary and then collect the White Card residence permit within 30 days of arrival at the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (NDGAP) office.

visas.name: Guest Investor Residence Permit (Golden Visa)
visas.description: The Guest Investor Residence Permit, also known as the Hungary Golden Visa, is a program for non-EU/EEA nationals who wish to obtain long-term residence in Hungary by making a qualifying investment. It allows investors and their close family members to live, work, and study in Hungary, and provides visa-free travel within the Schengen Area.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-EU/EEA national over 18 years of age with lawful funds, seeking long-term residence in Hungary through an investment in the national economy.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Permanent residency (PR) can be obtained after 3 years of living in Hungary, provided the applicant resides for at least 183 days a year. Hungarian citizenship can be applied for after 8 years of residing in Hungary, with absences not exceeding 45 days per year, and requires passing Hungarian language and history exams.
visas.renewal_conditions: The residence permit for guest investors can be extended for another 10 years, pre-conditioned on maintaining the investment. An application for extension must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the expiry date of the current permit.
visas.tax_implications: The program is associated with a 'favorable tax regime'. However, specific details beyond this general statement are not provided in the official sources found.
benefits: Residence permit issued for 10 years, renewable for another 10 years
No minimum physical stay requirement in Hungary
Visa-free movement within the Schengen Area
Right to live, study, and work in Hungary without restrictions
Includes spouse, children under 18, and dependent parents
required_documents: Full copy of a valid passport (with at least 12 months validity)
Two 3x4 cm photos (taken not earlier than one month ago)
Health insurance
Certificate of purchase of investment fund share OR proof of financial donation
Documents proving the purpose of residence
Documents proving means of subsistence (e.g., bank statement indicating cash balance, proof of legitimate income)
Documents proving accommodation
Written confirmation of the intention to fulfill the investment condition (if applicable)
CV for each family member over 18
Marriage certificate (if applicable)
Birth certificates (if applicable)
Filled-in residence permit form
application_process_steps: Choose an investment method and provide scanned passport copy for preliminary due diligence
Apply for a Guest Investor Visa at a Hungarian consulate abroad, submit biometrics, and pay the consular fee
Receive Guest Investor Visa (valid for up to 6 months, allowing multiple entries)
Travel to Hungary and complete the chosen investment within 93 days of first entry
Submit the residence permit application online via the Enter Hungary platform (within 30 days of first entry with visa, or within 93 days of first entry if visa-exempt)
Appear in person at the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (NDGAP) to provide fingerprints, photograph, sample signature, and pay the processing fee

visas.name: Residence Permit for the Purpose of Study (D-type visa)
visas.description: The Residence Permit for the Purpose of Study (often initiated by a D-type visa) allows non-EU/EEA citizens to reside in Hungary for long-term academic studies. The D-type visa serves as a single-entry permit to enter Hungary, after which applicants must apply for the actual residence permit with the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (NDGAP) within Hungary.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EEA citizens accepted into a full-time study program at a recognized Hungarian public educational institution or a state-recognized higher education institution for studies exceeding 90 days.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Upon successful completion of studies, graduates can apply for a 'residence permit for seeking a job or starting a business' which allows a stay of up to 9 months. This interim permit can then be converted to a residence permit based on gainful activity (employment or business). After 3 years of continuous legal residence in Hungary on a relevant permit (e.g., work permit), individuals may apply for permanent residency. Citizenship may be pursued after 8 years of permanent residency, subject to Hungarian language and history tests.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must hold a valid residence permit, reside in Hungary for at least 90 days in any 180-day period, provide updated proof of funds, current health insurance, proof of academic progress, and a passport with sufficient validity. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 30 days before the current permit expires.
benefits: Legal residency in Hungary for the duration of studies, renewable for academic progression.
Ability to travel within the Schengen Area after obtaining the residence permit.
Opportunity to work part-time (up to 30 hours/week) during studies and full-time (up to 90 days/year) during academic breaks.
Path to apply for a job-seeking or business-starting residence permit after graduation, which can lead to permanent residency.
Access to quality education within Hungarian institutions.
required_documents: Official acceptance letter from a recognized Hungarian educational institution
Valid passport (valid for at least 6 months beyond the intended stay and with at least two blank pages)
Proof of sufficient financial means for living expenses (e.g., bank statements, scholarship letter, sponsor declaration)
Proof of accommodation in Hungary (e.g., dormitory confirmation, rental contract)
Proof of health insurance covering the full stay in Hungary
Proof of tuition payment (or scholarship covering tuition)
Evidence of language proficiency suitable for the study program (if applicable)
Completed D-type visa application form
Two recent passport-sized photos (Schengen specifications)
Clean criminal record certificate from home country (and any country of recent residence), often requiring certified translation
Travel arrangements (e.g., one-way ticket for visa application, if required)
Birth certificate (certified and translated, if required by consulate)
Parental consent/non-objection letter for applicants under 18 years of age
application_process_steps: Accept an offer of admission from a recognized Hungarian university.
Gather all required documents as specified by the Hungarian consulate/embassy.
Book an appointment at the nearest Hungarian embassy or consulate in your country of nationality or habitual residence.
Submit the D-type visa application in person at the scheduled appointment, including biometrics.
Wait for the D-type visa decision; processing typically takes 30-60 days.
Upon approval, travel to Hungary using the single-entry D-type visa, which is valid for up to 30 days of stay within 3 months of issuance.

Within 30 days of arrival in Hungary, register your address and apply for the Residence Permit for Study Purposes at the regional office of the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (NDGAP).
Receive your residence permit card, typically issued for 1-2 years and renewable for the duration of your studies.

visas.name: EU Blue Card
visas.description: The EU Blue Card in Hungary is a residence permit for highly qualified third-country nationals, allowing them to live and work in Hungary in positions requiring advanced professional qualifications. It aims to attract skilled workers from outside the EU and facilitate their mobility within the Union.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-EU citizens with a tertiary education degree or significant professional experience, who have a valid work contract or binding job offer for a highly qualified position in Hungary for at least 6 months, meeting the specified minimum salary threshold.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Blue Card holders may apply for Hungarian permanent residence after 3 years of continuous residence in Hungary. They can also apply for EU long-term resident status after 5 years of legal and continuous residence in the EU (with a special rule allowing 2 continuous years in Hungary plus 5 years with an EU Blue Card in any EU member state).
visas.renewal_conditions: Maintaining valid employment, fulfilling residence rules, and submitting complete documentation. Applications for renewal must be submitted at least 30 days before the current permit expires. The Blue Card's validity can be extended for up to 4 years at a time.
benefits: Right to work full-time in a high-skilled position in Hungary.
Long-term residence opportunities, with initial validity typically between 1 and 4 years.
Family reunification, allowing spouses and children to obtain residence permits and work rights.
Mobility within the EU, allowing relocation to another EU country under simpler conditions after a certain period.
Clear path to permanent residency in Hungary and potentially long-term EU residence status.
required_documents: Valid passport.
Valid work contract or binding job offer for highly qualified employment (at least 6 months duration, but typically one year).

Documents proving higher education or professional qualification (bachelor's or master's degree, or 3 years of relevant professional experience within the last 7 years for executive officers and ICT specialists).
Proof of means of subsistence (e.g., preliminary agreement, employment contract, document on regular income).
Proof of sickness insurance (or proof of having applied for it).
Proof of accommodation.
Biometric photos.
Criminal record certificate.
Visa application form (if applying from abroad and visa required).
Employer's supporting documents.
application_process_steps: Secure a job offer or employment contract for a highly qualified position in Hungary.
Compile all necessary documents, including passport, employment contract, qualifications, health insurance, and criminal record certificate.

Submit the application: either at a Hungarian diplomatic or consular foreign mission if applying from outside Hungary, or in Hungary (in person or via the Enter Hungary platform) if legally residing or holding an EU Blue Card from another Member State.
Pay the administrative service fee.
Attend any required appointments, interviews, or biometric sessions.
Receive the decision and, if approved, the EU Blue Card and residence permit are issued.

visas.name: Hungarian Card
visas.description: The Hungarian Card (Nemzeti Kártya or Magyar Kártya) is a long-term residence permit introduced in 2024 for third-country nationals, designed to facilitate long-term residency and professional integration in Hungary. It combines work authorization and residence rights, aiming to attract professionals and business leaders.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for highly skilled professionals (e.g., IT specialists, engineers, natural sciences), professional athletes, coaches, performers, film production workers, and owners/managing directors of Hungarian companies who perform actual work in Hungary.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 3 years of continuous legal residence on the Hungarian Card, holders can apply for permanent residence (National Residence Card, valid for 10 years). Obtaining permanent residence may require passing an exam on basic Hungarian language and constitutional values. After 8 years of continuous permanent residence, it is possible to apply for Hungarian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain the grounds for residence (e.g., continue to run a business or work in Hungary in accordance with stated qualifications)
benefits: Legal right to work and reside in Hungary without a separate work permit
Initial validity of 3 years, renewable for another 3 years
Path to permanent residence after 3 years of continuous residence
Visa-free travel within the Schengen Area for up to 90 days in a 180-day period
Family reunification is allowed for spouse and minor children
required_documents: Valid passport (valid at least two years beyond application date for D visa)
Passport-size photograph
Completed residence permit application form
Proof of employment or business activity (e.g., preliminary employment agreement from a Hungarian employer, work contract, or incorporation documents for business owners)
Proof of financial solvency (e.g., bank statement for the last 3-6 months with a balance of at least €10,000, or certificate of income)
Residential lease agreement or title deed (proof of accommodation)
Proof of professional qualifications (e.g., BSc or MSc degrees in specified fields, professional certificates)
Health insurance (public or private)
Criminal record certificate
application_process_steps: Determine the basis for a residence permit (employment with a Hungarian company or registering a legal entity) and prepare documents.

Submit an application for a Category D visa at a Hungarian consulate in the applicant's country of permanent residence (or directly in Hungary via Enter Hungary if eligible, e.g., for non-visa nationals already in Hungary).
Undergo application review by the Migration Service, which verifies authenticity of documents, financial solvency, and legality of property.
If approved, obtain a Category D visa valid for 90 days.
Enter Hungary and personally apply for the plastic residence card at the immigration office, providing biometric data.
Receive the plastic residence permit card (typically within 3 weeks of biometric submission).

visas.name: Guest Worker Permit
visas.description: The 'Guest Worker Permit' in Hungary was a temporary work and residence permit designed for certain non-EU/EEA nationals to address labor shortages in key sectors such as manufacturing, construction, agriculture, and logistics. It allowed holders to live and work legally in Hungary for a specific job and employer for a limited duration. **As of June 6, 2026, new applications for this permit are no longer being accepted because no third countries are currently designated as eligible under the revised framework.** Existing permits remain valid, and applications submitted and paid for by June 5, 2026, will be processed and may be extended under previous rules.
visas.target_applicant: The program *was* primarily for non-EU/EEA nationals from specific countries (e.g., Georgia, Armenia, Philippines as of 2025) who secured a formal job offer from a government-certified strategic partner or licensed labor rental agency in Hungary, for positions in sectors facing workforce shortages. However, as new applications are suspended, there are currently no eligible nationalities.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Time spent under this permit does not count toward permanent residency or citizenship requirements in Hungary.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit can be extended once for an additional year, under the same employer, up to a maximum total stay of three years. Applicants must remain employed with the same certified company, continue to meet all labor law requirements, and stay within the approved job and sector scope. The renewal application must be submitted at least 40 days prior to the current permit's expiry via the Enter Hungary platform.
benefits: Allows legal employment and residence in Hungary for the duration of the permit for a specific job and employer.
Holders receive basic workplace protections under local labor law, including fair wages, standard working hours, and access to healthcare (typically through employer-contributed insurance).
Authorizes travel across the Schengen Area.
Offers a relatively streamlined application process with shorter processing times compared to some other permits.
required_documents: A valid passport, with at least 12 months of validity remaining.
An employment contract from an eligible Hungarian employer.
Proof of housing in Hungary (e.g., rental contract or employer-provided accommodation).
A criminal record certificate from the home country.
Proof of medical insurance covering the stay in Hungary.
Completed application form.
Proof of administrative service fee payment.
Documents proving qualifications relevant to the job.
application_process_steps: Secure a formal job offer from a government-certified strategic partner or licensed labor rental agency in Hungary for a position in a sector facing workforce shortages.

Prepare all necessary documents, including a valid passport, employment contract, proof of housing, criminal record certificate, medical insurance, completed application form, and proof of fee payment.
Submit the application at a Hungarian consulate in the country of origin or via the online 'Enter Hungary' platform.
Attend any required appointments, interviews, or biometric data collection sessions.
Await the processing of the application and receive the decision.

visas.name: Guest Self-Employment Permit (Residence Permit for the Purpose of Gainful Activity)
visas.description: The Guest Self-Employment Permit, also known as the Residence Permit for the Purpose of Gainful Activity, is designed for third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA citizens) who intend to establish and operate a business, work as a freelancer, or serve as a managing director of a company in Hungary. It allows applicants to legally reside in Hungary and conduct independent professional activities, contributing to the local economy.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are freelancers, independent contractors, small-scale farmers/producers, service providers working independently in Hungary, or managing directors/entrepreneurs establishing and actively managing a Hungarian business entity.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of this permit can apply for a National Permanent Residence Card after 5 years of continuous legal residence in Hungary. After 8 years, they may be eligible for citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew, applicants must hold a valid Guest Self-Employment permit, have resided in Hungary for at least 90 days in any 180-day period, fulfill regular reporting obligations to the immigration authorities, and continue to meet the original eligibility conditions, including maintaining the required income threshold.
visas.tax_implications: Tax residents in Hungary are subject to income tax on their worldwide income at a flat rate of 15%. Capital gains, dividends, interests, and rental income are generally taxed at a standard rate. Non-residents are only taxed on income arising from Hungarian sources.
benefits: Legal residency in Hungary and the EU for up to 3 years.
Ability to work as a registered self-employed person/sole proprietor or serve as a managing director of a Hungarian company.
No investment or donation requirement.
Path to permanent residency after 5 years and citizenship after 8 years.
Potential for favorable tax treatment as a Hungarian tax resident.
required_documents: Completed and signed application form with proof of administrative service fee payment.
Valid passport (valid for at least 3 months beyond permit expiry).
One recent facial photograph.
Proof of purpose of residence (e.g., private entrepreneurial license, business plan, registration number, business declaration, contracts, tax certificate).
Proof of financial means (e.g., bank statements, tax returns, income certificates, proof of net wealth, savings account statement).
Proof of accommodation in Hungary (e.g., rental agreement, property ownership, reservation of accommodation).
Proof of comprehensive health insurance covering Hungary.
Travel documents evidencing means of exit (e.g., valid passport or permits for return to country of origin, valid ticket or sufficient funds for ticket).
Certificate attesting to a clean police record.
Certificate from the tax authority stating that the annual income from self-employment exceeds 24 times the current minimum wage.
Certificate stating no outstanding tax or contribution debts.
Detailed declaration of business activity for executive roles, demonstrating essential residence in Hungary and sufficient income for the business's subsistence.
application_process_steps: Check eligibility requirements and confirm qualification for the visa category.
Gather all required documents, including financial proof, insurance, identity documents, and a detailed business plan.
Submit the application through the official immigration portal (Enter Hungary) or at a Hungarian consulate/embassy in the country of origin/legal residence if applying from abroad.
Attend any required appointments, interviews, or biometrics sessions.
Receive the decision on the application.
If approved, prepare for the move to Hungary and fulfill ongoing reporting obligations to the immigration office (OIF) via the E-Paper platform.

visas.name: Residence Permit for Family Reunification (D-type visa)
visas.description: The Residence Permit for Family Reunification in Hungary allows third-country nationals to join their family members who are legally residing in Hungary, provided the sponsor holds a qualifying residence permit or is a Hungarian citizen. This permit enables family members to live, study, and under certain conditions, work in Hungary, and travel within the Schengen area.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for spouses (including registered partners), minor children (under 18), dependent parents, and in some specific cases, dependent siblings or ascendants of individuals who hold a valid Hungarian residence permit or are Hungarian citizens.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five years of continuous legal residence in Hungary with a family reunification residence permit, family members may become eligible to apply for an EC long-term residence permit or other forms of permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The validity period may not exceed that of the applicant's travel document or the sponsor's residence permit. The applicant must have resided in Hungary for at least 90 days in any 180-day period (not applicable for family members of guest investors). An application for extension must be submitted no more than 90 days and no later than 30 days before the current permit's expiry. The dissolution of marriage or death of the sponsor must be reported to the immigration authority within 30 days.
benefits: Legal right to reside in Hungary with family.
Access to education in Hungary.
Possibility to work in Hungary under specific conditions (e.g., single application procedure or separate work permit).
Travel within the Schengen area for short stays once the residence permit is issued.
Potential path to permanent residency after 5 years.
required_documents: Fully completed residence permit application form and specific family reunification questionnaire.
Valid passport (valid for at least 3 months beyond the intended period of stay).
One recent passport-sized color photograph.

Proof of family relationship (e.g., original marriage certificate, birth certificate, adoption documents; if for a Hungarian citizen spouse, a domestically registered Hungarian marriage certificate is required. DNA analysis may be requested to prove family links).
Proof of accommodation in Hungary (e.g., residential lease contract, document on accommodation by courtesy, document in proof of ownership of property).

Proof of sufficient financial means for subsistence in Hungary (e.g., bank statements, employer's certificate of regular income, work contract and salary slips for the past six months, tax authority certificate, demonstrating continuous and predictable income).
Proof of comprehensive health insurance covering all healthcare services or documents proving ability to cover the costs of such services.
Documents proving conditions for exit (e.g., valid return ticket or sufficient funds to cover travel costs).
Consent of the parent or legal representative for minor applicants.
If combining with employment: preliminary employment agreement or document on legal relationship of employment.
application_process_steps: Verify eligibility based on the sponsor's residence status and the family relationship type.
Gather all required documents, ensuring they are in Hungarian or English, with certified translations if necessary.

Submit the application in person at a Hungarian diplomatic mission or consulate in the country of nationality/habitual residence, or at a regional directorate of the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (NDGAP) in Hungary if legally present, or electronically via the Enter Hungary platform.
Attend an interview and provide biometric data if requested by the authorities.
If applying from abroad, upon approval, receive a D-type entry visa, which is a single-entry visa valid for 3 months and authorizing a stay of up to 30 days.
Travel to Hungary using the D-type visa and collect the residence permit document from the NDGAP office within 30 days of arrival, and register the address of accommodation.

visas.name: Residence Permit for Official Purposes
visas.description: The Residence Permit for Official Purposes in Hungary is issued to third-country nationals who intend to reside in Hungary for official duties. This includes individuals enjoying diplomatic or other privileges and immunities under international law, members of official delegations, journalists, or participants in international programs (education, science, culture, professional training), as well as staff of scientific, educational, and cultural institutions operating under international conventions. Family members of those enjoying privileges and immunities are also eligible.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals with diplomatic status, members of foreign official delegations, journalists, or those involved in international educational, scientific, or cultural cooperation, and their eligible family members.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Temporary resident status with this permit can generally lead to permanent residency (National Residence Card) after at least 3 years of continuous legal residence in Hungary. Permanent residency allows for indefinite stay and eventually may lead to Hungarian citizenship, subject to specific conditions including periods of absence from Hungary.
visas.renewal_conditions: The validity period may be extended in accordance with the duration of the official service or training, not exceeding 3 years. The applicant must be a holder of a valid residence permit at the time of application submission and must have resided within the territory of Hungary with their residence permit for at least 90 days in any 180-day period. The extension application must be submitted no more than 90 days prior to the expiry and no later than 30 days before the expiry of the current permit.
benefits: Legal residence in Hungary for official duties.
Ability to travel visa-free within the Schengen Area.
Access to Hungarian state health insurance (implied for residents).
Potential path to permanent residency and citizenship after meeting continuous residency requirements.
Family members can be included.
required_documents: Valid passport (valid for at least 3 months beyond the intended stay).
Two passport-size color photos (not older than 6 months).
Wholly and legibly completed, signed residence permit application form.
Supporting documents of the purpose of stay (e.g., document proving diplomatic privileges, certificate/declaration from a foreign state/organization/institution).
Supporting documents of accommodation in Hungary (e.g., lease agreement, ownership document).
Supporting documents of subsistence (e.g., bank statements, income certificate, sponsor documents).
Proof of comprehensive health insurance or financial resources to cover health services.
Document certifying a clean criminal record (for National Residence Card, likely required generally, especially for those over 14).
application_process_steps: Complete the application form for a residence permit for official purposes.
Gather all mandatory supporting documents, including valid passport, photos, proof of purpose, accommodation, subsistence, and health insurance.
Submit the application before a diplomatic or consular foreign mission of Hungary in your country of nationality or habitual residence, or electronically via the 'Enter Hungary' platform.
Pay the administrative service fee (EUR 60 if submitted abroad, HUF 18,000 if submitted in Hungary).

If applying electronically, visit the competent regional directorate of the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (NDGAP) within 15 days of submission to provide biometric data (facial photograph, fingerprints) and signature specimen.
The competent authority will decide on the application within the procedural administration period.

visas.name: Residence Permit for Medical Treatment
visas.description: The Residence Permit for Medical Treatment in Hungary is designed for third-country nationals who intend to receive medical treatment in Hungary. It also permits individuals to accompany their minor child or a family member who requires support for medical treatment in Hungary. This permit allows the holder to reside in Hungary for the duration of the medical treatment.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA citizens and stateless persons) planning to stay in Hungary for medical treatment, or accompanying a minor child or a dependent family member who requires medical treatment.
visas.path_to_residency_description: During the validity period and after the expiry date of a residence permit for medical treatment, it is not permitted to apply for another type of residence permit in Hungary. Holders of this permit may not be granted a national residence card (permanent residency).
visas.renewal_conditions: The application for extension must be submitted no more than 90 days and no later than 30 days prior to the expiry date of the current residence permit. The conditions that served as the basis for issuing the original residence permit must remain unchanged.
benefits: Right to reside in Hungary for the period of medical treatment.
Visa-free travel within the Schengen Area for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
Access to high-quality healthcare services in Hungary.
required_documents: Duly filled and signed application form for residence permit and Appendix (Medical Treatment specific).
Valid passport (valid for at least 3 months beyond the authorized stay, issued within the previous 10 years, with at least 2 blank pages).
Two recent passport-sized color photographs.
Official document/certificate from the host medical institution detailing the medical treatment, expected duration, and confirmation of coverage from the applicant's side.
Proof of accommodation in Hungary (e.g., residential lease contract, owner statement, proof of property ownership, or reservation/payment for accommodation).
Proof of sufficient financial resources (e.g., up-to-date personal bank account statement for the last 6 months, certificate of regular income from abroad, proof of other assets).

Travel assistance policy or health insurance valid for the Schengen area with minimum coverage of €30,000, or proof of comprehensive health insurance covering all healthcare services in Hungary, or proof of ability to cover healthcare costs from available means of subsistence.
Round-trip flight ticket or reservation indicating the complete itinerary.
Police Clearance Certificate.
If accompanying a family member: official document proving the family relationship.
If the applicant is a minor: parental consent (public or private document with full evidential force, provided with a Hungarian or English translation).
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring they are in Hungarian or English, or officially translated.
Submit the application in person at a Hungarian diplomatic or consular foreign mission in the country of nationality or habitual residence (if applying from abroad).

Alternatively, if already in Hungary under special circumstances, submit the application in person at the competent regional directorate of the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (NDGAP) or electronically via the Enter Hungary platform if using a legal representative.
Pay the administrative service fee (HUF 18,000 if submitted in Hungary, or EUR 60 if submitted abroad).
Attend an interview, if requested, and provide biometric data (facial photograph and fingerprints).
The competent immigration authority will adopt a decision on the application within 21 days.

visas.name: Residence Permit for Research
visas.description: This permit is for third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA citizens) who wish to enter Hungary to carry out a research project under a hosting agreement with an accredited Hungarian research organization. It allows for legal stay and work related to the research activity.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals seeking to conduct scientific research in Hungary under a hosting agreement with a research organization accredited by the National Research, Development and Innovation Office.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Upon successful completion of the research project, holders of a Residence Permit for Research may apply for a residence permit for the purpose of seeking employment or starting a business, provided the prospective job or business aligns with the level of their completed research [10, 18].
visas.renewal_conditions: The residence permit may be extended for a period corresponding to the duration of the hosting agreement, not exceeding two years at a time. The application for extension must be submitted at least 30 days before the expiry of the current permit. The permit cannot be extended if the holder has left Hungary for more than 90 days within any 180-day period [3, 5].
visas.tax_implications: Standard Hungarian resident tax rules apply. No specific tax exemptions or special treatments are mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Permission to reside and conduct research in Hungary for up to two years initially.
Possibility for family members to join the researcher in Hungary.
Path to apply for a job-seeking or business-starting residence permit after completing research.
Opportunity for long-term mobility within the EU for researchers already holding a research permit from another EU Member State.
required_documents: Duly filled and signed application form for residence permit and Appendix 8 (Research or long-term mobility of researchers) [8, 19]
Valid travel document (passport) with at least two blank pages and validity extending at least three months beyond the intended stay [3, 7, 8, 9]
Two passport-sized photographs (not older than 3 months) [7, 9, 12]
Hosting agreement concluded with an accredited Hungarian research organization [3, 6, 8, 9, 10]

Proof of sufficient means of subsistence (e.g., income certificate from employer/tax authority, bank account statement demonstrating regular income or savings to cover living, accommodation, return travel, and healthcare costs) [7, 8, 10]
Proof of accommodation in Hungary (e.g., residential lease contract, document on accommodation by courtesy, or real estate sales contract) [7, 8]
Proof of comprehensive health insurance or sufficient financial resources to cover healthcare services [7, 8, 10]
Written commitment from the research organization to reimburse expulsion costs if the researcher lacks financial means [3, 6]
Police Clearance Certificate [8]
Long and short-term mobility plan, indicating planned duration and dates of mobility (if applicable for EU mobility) [3]
application_process_steps: Ensure that the hosting research organization in Hungary is accredited by the National Research, Development and Innovation Office [5, 15].
Conclude a hosting agreement with the accredited research organization [3, 8].
Gather all necessary supporting documents, including proof of purpose of stay, means of subsistence, accommodation, and health insurance [7, 8].

Submit the application: either online via the 'Enter Hungary' platform, in person at a regional directorate of the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (if already in Hungary), or at a Hungarian consulate/embassy in the applicant's country of residence or nationality if applying from abroad [3, 4, 5, 9].
Pay the application fee (EUR 110 if submitted abroad, HUF 39,000 in person in Hungary, or HUF 26,000 via 'Enter Hungary' platform) [3, 5, 13].
Await the decision; the processing time can take up to 60 days [13, 17].
If approved, collect the residence permit, typically from the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing after arriving in Hungary [9, 12].

visas.name: Residence Permit for Traineeship/Internship
visas.description: This permit is for third-country nationals coming to Hungary to undertake a formal traineeship or internship. It allows individuals to gain work experience and build professional skills within an approved Hungarian host organization.
visas.target_applicant: Recent graduates (within two years of obtaining a higher education degree) or current students pursuing higher education in a non-EU country who have secured a formal traineeship contract with an approved Hungarian host organization.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This permit does not lead to long-term residence or employment in Hungary. Holders cannot apply for permanent residency based on this permit.
visas.renewal_conditions: This residence permit cannot be extended or renewed. An application for a residence permit under another legal title is not allowed during its validity or after its expiry.
benefits: Opportunity to gain professional work experience in Hungary.
Valid for short-term stays in Hungary for the purpose of traineeship.
Allows travel within the Schengen area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
Streamlined application process through Hungarian embassies/consulates or the Enter Hungary platform.
required_documents: Valid passport/travel document

Traineeship contract with the host organization, including: description of the program, educational objective/learning components, duration, conditions for placement and supervision, number of practical hours, legal relationship between trainee and host, and host's declaration of responsibility for subsistence and accommodation costs.
Proof of higher education degree obtained within two years preceding the application or proof of ongoing higher education studies relevant to the traineeship.
Evidence of necessary language skills for the traineeship.
Proof of means of subsistence (e.g., bank account statements, employer's certificate of regular income, host organization's declaration of coverage).
Proof of accommodation in Hungary.
Health insurance covering the entire duration of stay.
Written commitment from the host organization to reimburse expulsion costs if the trainee overstays and lacks financial resources.
application_process_steps: Secure a traineeship contract with an approved Hungarian host organization that meets the specified criteria.
Gather all required documents, including proof of education, language skills, financial means, accommodation, and health insurance.

Submit the application: either at a Hungarian embassy or consulate in your country of nationality or habitual residence (for non-visa-exempt travelers), or electronically via the 'Enter Hungary' platform, or in person at a regional directorate of the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (for visa-exempt travelers already in Hungary).
Pay the administrative service fee.
Attend an appointment to provide facial photograph, fingerprints, and signature specimen if applying online or in person.
Await the decision on the application, which typically takes between 21 and 60 days.

Citizenship by Descent.desc:
Hungarian citizenship is based on the principle of *jus sanguinis* (right of blood). Individuals can acquire citizenship if at least one parent was a Hungarian citizen at the time of their birth, regardless of birthplace.
Lineage can be traced through grandparents or even great-grandparents, provided direct ancestral links are proven with official documents such as birth and marriage certificates, and the applicant demonstrates basic Hungarian language knowledge and has a clean criminal record.

Naturalization.desc:
Standard naturalization requires 8 years of continuous residence in Hungary, a clean criminal record, a stable livelihood, good character, and passing a test in basic constitutional studies in Hungarian.
Reduced residency periods apply for certain groups: 5 years for those born in Hungary, who settled before age 18, or who are stateless.
Refugees can apply after 3 years.
Investors under the Guest Investor Program (reintroduced 2024) can obtain a 10-year residence permit, potentially leading to citizenship application after 8 years of continuous residence.

Birthright.desc: Hungary generally follows *jus sanguinis*, meaning birth in Hungary to foreign parents does not automatically grant Hungarian citizenship unless the child would otherwise be stateless.

Spouse and Family.desc:
Marriage to a Hungarian citizen can significantly shorten the naturalization period.
Applicants may apply after 3 years of continuous residence in Hungary if married to a Hungarian citizen for at least 3 years.
Alternatively, citizenship can be obtained after 10 years of marriage to a Hungarian citizen without a residency requirement, or after 5 years of marriage if the couple has at least one child together (also without a residency requirement).
Applicants must have a clean criminal record and pass a basic constitutional knowledge exam.

tax_advice:
- **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** A flat rate of 15% applies to both residents and non-residents.
- **Corporate Tax:** One of the lowest in the EU at 9%.
- **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The highest in Europe at 27%, with reduced rates of 18% (hospitality, internet, dairy) and 5% (medicines, books, fresh meats).
- **Social Contributions:** Employees contribute 18.5% on gross salary (10% pension, 4% health, 3% cash benefits, 1.5% unemployment). Employers contribute 14.5% (13% social tax, 1.5% training contribution).
- **Tax Benefits (Changes from Jan 1, 2025):** Eligibility for the family allowance, first-time married couples allowance, and under-25s allowance is restricted. As of January 1, 2025, these benefits generally cannot be applied to the salaries of most third-country nationals, except for citizens of EEA countries and non-EEA countries bordering Hungary (Serbia, Ukraine).
- **Capital Gains Tax:** Taxed at the ordinary income tax rate of 15%.
- **Inheritance Tax:** No wealth tax. Direct heirs (children, spouse) are fully exempt from inheritance duties. The standard rate is 18%, reduced to 9% for residential property.
- **International Agreements:** Hungary has an extensive income tax treaty network with over 73 countries. However, the U.S.-Hungary tax treaty was terminated effective January 1, 2024, potentially creating double taxation risks for U.S. citizens, though a social security totalization agreement remains in force.
local_tips:
- **Cost of Living:** Overall significantly lower than Western Europe. A single person's monthly expenses average €616-€863 (HUF 250,000-350,000) including rent in Budapest, while a family of four can expect around €2,700 (HUF 1,090,000).
- **Rent:** Budapest is the most expensive, with a furnished one-bedroom flat in the city center averaging €486-€543 (HUF 197,000-220,000) per month. Rents in smaller cities can be 30-50% lower.
- **Language:** Hungarian is a challenging language. While English is spoken in Budapest, especially in expat communities and tourism, learning basic Hungarian is highly recommended for daily life and integration, particularly outside the capital.
- **Safety:** Hungary is a very safe country with low crime rates. Petty theft like pickpocketing can occur in crowded tourist areas of Budapest.
- **Registration & Residency:** For long-term stays (over 90 days), non-EU citizens need a residence permit. Options include work permits, student visas, guest investor residency (reintroduced in 2024, offering a 10-year permit for investments starting at €250,000 in real estate funds), or the 'White Card' digital nomad visa.
- **Cultural Knowledge Exam:** As of January 1, 2025, foreign nationals applying for a National Residence Card or EU Residence Card will need to pass a cultural knowledge exam in Hungarian to demonstrate social coexistence.
- **Bureaucracy:** Expats often cite bureaucracy as a significant challenge.
